properties.natural_language: Before processing a SET_CODE transaction (type 0x05), the transaction MUST undergo full authorization list validation including: chain ID verification (must match current chain or be 0 for universal), nonce bounds check (nonce < U64.MAX), ECDSA signature recovery for each authorization, account nonce matching, and existing code validation (empty or valid delegation code only).

Before accepting an authorization signature during EOA delegation, the signature parameters MUST be validated: y_parity must be exactly 0 or 1, r and s values must be within secp256k1 curve order (0 < r < n, 0 < s < n), and the signing hash must be correctly computed as keccak256(0x05 || RLP(chain_id, address, nonce)).

After successfully setting delegation code (0xef0100 + target_address), the authority account's nonce MUST be incremented by exactly 1, ensuring that the same authorization cannot be replayed even if the delegation is later cleared.

Delegation code MUST maintain exactly 23 bytes format: 3-byte marker (0xef0100) followed by 20-byte target address. Any code that does not match this exact format (length != 23 OR does not start with 0xef0100) MUST be treated as non-delegation code.

Before allowing delegation to NULL_ADDRESS (0x0000...0000), the system MUST verify that the result will be empty code (length 0), effectively revoking the delegation and restoring the account to standard EOA behavior without residual delegation state.

For any authorization that fails validation (chain ID mismatch, nonce bounds violation, signature recovery failure, account nonce mismatch, or invalid existing code), the authorization MUST be skipped without raising an error, preserving the ability to batch multiple authorizations where some may succeed and others fail gracefully.

Before accepting a raw block from the P2P network, the block header MUST undergo full RLP decoding and validation including: parent_hash verification against known parent, state_root matching post-execution state trie, transactions_root, receipts_root, withdrawals_root correctness, and requests_hash verification as SHA2-256 commitment. Malformed RLP MUST be rejected immediately.

Before processing withdrawals from the consensus layer via Engine API, each withdrawal (index, validator_index, address, amount) MUST be validated for: sequential withdrawal indices, valid Ethereum addresses, correct Gwei amounts, and withdrawals_root MUST match the Merkle-Patricia trie commitment in the header. The CL provides the data via authenticated Engine API but content validation remains EL responsibility.

After all withdrawals in a block are processed, the computed withdrawals_root MUST match the commitment in the block header. Each withdrawal MUST have resulted in the recipient address balance being increased by the exact amount specified in Gwei, with state trie updates persisted atomically.

Before including the requests_hash in a block header, all protocol requests generated during block execution MUST be collected, serialized in deterministic format, and hashed using SHA2-256 (not Keccak256). The CL provides the header but the EL MUST independently recompute and verify this hash.

Transaction receipt encoding MUST match transaction type: Legacy (type 0) has no prefix, Access List (type 1) uses 0x01 prefix, Fee Market (type 2) uses 0x02 prefix, Blob (type 3) uses 0x03 prefix, and SetCode (type 4/0x04) uses 0x04 prefix. Type prefix MUST be prepended before RLP encoding for all non-legacy types.

The ommers field in Prague blocks MUST always be present as an empty tuple with ommers_hash equal to the hash of an empty list, maintaining backwards compatibility with pre-Proof-of-Stake formats. Non-empty ommers MUST be rejected as invalid.

Before executing the Capella fork upgrade at epoch boundary (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 AND epoch == CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH), the system MUST verify both conditions are met within process_slots. The upgrade MUST execute atomically: either the full state upgrade completes (initializing withdrawal fields, upgrading ExecutionPayloadHeader, updating fork version) or none of it does.

After completing the Capella fork upgrade, the beacon state MUST have: next_withdrawal_index=0, next_withdrawal_validator_index=0, historical_summaries=[], ExecutionPayloadHeader with withdrawals_root field initialized to empty root, previous_version set to pre-fork current_version, current_version=CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION, and epoch=CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH.

All nodes in the network MUST agree on CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH (194048) and CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION (0x03000000). Any node with different fork epoch or version values will fork the chain at a different point, causing a permanent chain split.

When slots are skipped around the CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH boundary, process_slots MUST iterate through all skipped slots and trigger the fork upgrade at the exact epoch boundary slot (first slot where slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 AND computed epoch == CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH), regardless of how many slots were skipped.

Before applying the fork upgrade during historical sync when a node first syncs to a post-Capella chain, process_slots MUST apply the upgrade when crossing the fork epoch boundary, identical to live operation behavior. There MUST be no special handling for historical vs live fork transitions.

Before accepting a SignedExecutionPayloadBid from a builder, the proposer MUST validate: (1) builder is active in registry verified via finalized checkpoint, (2) builder balance >= bid_value + MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT + pending_withdrawals, (3) BLS signature verification succeeds, (4) slot/parent_block_hash/randao match current context, (5) blob commitment count within MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK, (6) parent block fullness (previous bid fulfilled with payload delivery).

Before delivering an ExecutionPayloadEnvelope, the builder MUST provide payload data and blobs that match the accepted bid commitments: builder signature verification, payload consistency with bid (matching builder_index, slot, parent), and blob data matching KZG commitments. The PTC attestation will determine whether builder receives payment.

After the PTC (512 validators) attests to payload availability and the BUILDER_PAYMENT_THRESHOLD (6/10 quorum) is met at epoch boundary, the builder MUST receive payment from their balance. If the threshold is not met or PTC majority attests payload absence, payment MUST be withheld.

After builder voluntary exit is initiated (with zero pending withdrawals), the builder MUST enter exiting state with withdrawable_epoch = current_epoch + MIN_BUILDER_WITHDRAWABILITY_DELAY (64 epochs). Once withdrawable_epoch is reached, the builder's remaining balance MUST be refunded to their execution address, and the builder index becomes available for reuse (but the pubkey cannot be reactivated).

Withdrawal processing at epoch boundary MUST follow strict priority order: (1) builder pending withdrawals, (2) partial validator withdrawals (excess balance), (3) builder sweep withdrawals (max 16384 per sweep), (4) validator sweep withdrawals. This deterministic order prevents withdrawal manipulation and ensures fair processing.

The BUILDER_INDEX_FLAG (2^40) MUST be applied via bitwise OR to builder indices to distinguish them from validator indices during withdrawal routing. Withdrawals MUST check this flag bit to correctly route funds to builder execution addresses vs validator withdrawal credentials. Manipulation of this encoding could redirect withdrawals to unintended recipients.

For proposer self-build mode, the bid_amount MUST be zero regardless of the proposer's withdrawal credentials. BLS signature verification MUST be skipped for self-builds. For external builder bids, BLS signature verification is REQUIRED and balance sufficiency checks MUST be enforced to prevent self-payment exploits.

Before processing a builder deposit, the BLS deposit signature MUST be verified. Builder deposits are processed immediately without a queue (no activation delay). Builder indices become reusable after full withdrawal completion, but the same pubkey MUST NOT be reactivated to prevent registry manipulation.

PTC selection MUST use balance-weighted selection from only active validators with non-zero effective balance. The PTC of 512 validators is assumed honest-majority. If a dishonest PTC majority exists, they could falsely attest payload absence (denying builder payment) or falsely attest presence (paying builders who didn't deliver). Partial availability (some blobs missing) MUST be treated as absence.

Before responding to an eth_chainId JSON-RPC request, the node MUST parse and validate the request format, retrieve the chain ID from the current head block configuration, and encode it as a 0x-prefixed hexadecimal string with no leading zeros (except for value 0 which is '0x0'). The response MUST reflect the correct chain ID from head block, not a cached or stale value.

If the current head block does not specify a chain ID (pre-EIP-155 blocks), the eth_chainId method MUST return an error indicating the method is unsupported for the current head block state, rather than returning a default or guessed chain ID value.

Before signing a transaction, wallet applications MUST query eth_chainId (not net_version, as network ID and chain ID may differ) to obtain the current chain ID and verify it matches the expected network. If chain ID mismatches the expected value, the wallet MUST warn the user they may be connected to the wrong network to prevent cross-chain replay attacks.

After obtaining the correct chain ID and verifying it matches the expected network, the wallet MUST include the chain ID in the transaction signature per EIP-155, resulting in a transaction that is replay-protected and cannot be replayed on chains with different chain IDs.

The chain ID returned by eth_chainId MUST remain constant during normal operation and MUST only change during hard forks that explicitly modify the chain ID. The chain ID MUST NOT change during block reorganizations. Nodes MUST NOT be compromised or misconfigured to return incorrect chain IDs, as this would lead to replay attacks or loss of funds.

When a contract invokes the MODEXP precompile (address 0x05) via CALL, the input data must be properly parsed to extract base_length, exp_length, and mod_length from the first 96 bytes, with zero-padding applied if input is shorter than required.

Before charging gas for MODEXP computation, the gas cost formula must compute complexity as max(base_length, mod_length) squared and iteration count from exponent bit length, ensuring the minimum gas cost is 200 regardless of input size.

If modulus is zero, MODEXP must return mod_length bytes of zeros; if both base and modulus are zero, it must return empty bytes. The computation must never proceed with modulus=0 through the normal pow(base, exp, mod) path.
After gas is charged for MODEXP, if the computed gas cost exceeds available gas, execution must revert to the out-of-gas state without performing the modular exponentiation computation.

The quadratic gas formula (complexity * iterations / 3) with minimum 200 gas must prevent memory exhaustion attacks by ensuring gas is exhausted before memory allocation for extremely large operand sizes can succeed.

After MODEXP computation completes, the result must be converted to big-endian bytes padded to exactly mod_length bytes before setting evm.output, ensuring consistent output format regardless of result magnitude.

When a user submits a transaction invoking a contract that uses BASEFEE, the base fee value must be read from the current block context (not user input), preventing user manipulation of the base fee value used in contract logic.

Before executing the BASEFEE opcode (0x48), the EVM must verify that at least 2 gas units (G_base) are available; if insufficient gas exists, execution must revert without pushing any value to the stack.

After fetching the BASEFEE opcode, the base fee value must be pushed to the stack as a 32-byte big-endian left-padded value, and exactly 2 gas units must be deducted before execution continues to the next opcode.

The base fee value returned by BASEFEE must be derived from the current block header and computed according to EIP-1559 rules, not arbitrarily set by block producers, ensuring contracts using BASEFEE for pricing cannot be manipulated through base fee tampering.
The base fee value must be available in the block context before any EVM execution begins, preventing circular dependencies where EVM execution results could influence base fee computation.

When the execution engine provides a payload and blobs_bundle via get_payload, the validator must verify that KZG commitments in the blobs_bundle match the actual blob data and that the blob count does not exceed MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK.

When a blob sidecar is received from the gossip network, the validator must verify that the blob index is within MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK bounds, the KZG proof matches the commitment, the Merkle inclusion proof links the commitment to the block body, and the signed block header is valid before accepting the sidecar.

After assembling the beacon block body with blob_kzg_commitments from blobs_bundle.commitments, the validator must construct BlobSidecars containing index, blob data, kzg_commitment, kzg_proof, signed_block_header, and kzg_commitment_inclusion_proof for each blob before broadcasting.

Each blob sidecar must be broadcast to the correct subnet determined by subnet_id = blob_index % BLOB_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT, ensuring proper distribution across the gossip network for data availability.
After a blob sidecar fails any validation check (invalid index, KZG proof mismatch, or invalid inclusion proof), it must transition to the rejected state and be discarded without further processing.

When serving blob sidecar sync requests from peers, validators must only serve sidecars that are within the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS retention window and have been fully validated, with rate limiting applied to prevent resource exhaustion.

Blob sidecars must be retained for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs from their slot, ensuring data availability for validators and sync requests during the mandatory retention period.

When a wallet browser extension injects provider code and dispatches eip6963:announceProvider events, DApps must freeze the EIP6963ProviderDetail object using Object.freeze() before processing to prevent prototype pollution and object modification attacks.

Before accepting a provider announcement, DApps must validate that the uuid field is UUIDv4 compliant, the rdns field is a valid RFC-1034 reverse domain name, and the icon is a valid RFC-2397 data URI with at least 96x96px resolution.
DApps must detect duplicate UUID values across multiple EIP6963ProviderInfo announcements as potential wallet impersonation attempts, transitioning to a suspicious state when duplicates are found.
After receiving provider announcements, DApps must render SVG wallet icons exclusively via tags (not inline SVG) to prevent execution of embedded JavaScript in malicious SVG data URIs.

DApp event listeners for eip6963:announceProvider must persist for the entire page lifetime (until navigation or unload), continuing to collect provider announcements even in single-page application contexts across route changes.

The rdns field should be treated as advisory only without authentication, as DApps cannot verify domain ownership; malicious extensions can claim any rdns value, requiring users to rely on visual cues and UUID uniqueness to identify legitimate wallets.

Before executing the EXTCODEHASH opcode (0x3f), the EVM must verify that at least 400 gas units are available; if insufficient gas exists, execution must revert to the out-of-gas state without performing the account lookup.

After reading an address from the stack for EXTCODEHASH, only the last 20 bytes must be used as the account address (ignoring the first 96 bits), and the state trie must be queried to determine account existence per EIP-161 emptiness rules.

EXTCODEHASH must return 0 for non-existent accounts or EIP-161 empty accounts (nonce=0, balance=0, no code), return keccak256('') for accounts with no code, and return keccak256(code) for accounts with bytecode, ensuring consistent distinction between account states.

The EIP-161 emptiness check must account for transaction-local state changes including SELFDESTRUCT operations and CREATE collisions, ensuring EXTCODEHASH sees consistent pre-SELFDESTRUCT state within the same transaction until transaction completion.

The code hash returned by EXTCODEHASH must be the keccak256 hash of the exact bytecode stored in the state trie at the queried address, relying on collision resistance to ensure code identity verification cannot be bypassed by finding different code with the same hash.
After computing the EXTCODEHASH result (0, empty hash, or code hash), it must be pushed to the EVM stack as a 32-byte value and exactly 400 gas must be consumed before opcode execution completes.
